Thanks for the report! This is an automated first-pass triage; a maintainer will make the final call.

**Reproduction:** Black 25.11.0 (default flags): reformatted, no error. Black 26.1.0 (latest on the issue date): same output. Both runs passed Black's default `--safe` AST-equivalence check.

**Assessment:** The reformatting only splits lines and does not change meaning. A conditional expression has lower precedence than `==`, so `my_var == 999 if abc == "TEST" else 0` already parses as `(my_var == 999) if abc == "TEST" else 0`. When `abc == "TEST"` it evaluates to `my_var == 999`, not `my_var == 0`. Black's AST check would have refused to write the file if the formatted code were not equivalent to the source. The example in the report is therefore not a semantic change.

**Next step:** If you meant `my_var == (999 if abc == "TEST" else 0)`, the parentheses must be in your source, because Black does not add parentheses that change grouping. If you saw a different behaviour, please share a snippet where the AST differs, or where a real program behaves differently. See [the Black code style](https://black.readthedocs.io/en/stable/the_black_code_style/current_style.html).
